job.title: Account Manager - Medical Devices
job.description:
THE COMPANY YOU WOULD BE JOINING
  • This is an Australian, family-owned business dedicated to enhancing medical care in Australia.
  • They specialise in crafting medical devices customised to meet specific clinical requirements.
  • With a history spanning over a decade, they have been developing and producing devices that streamline the work of healthcare professionals and caregivers.
WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU?
  • Embark on a journey of mentorship and inspiration, guided by one of the industry's most exceptional managers.
  • Join forces with a passionate team dedicated to these exceptional products.
  • Cultivate enduring relationships with nurses and clinical staff to truly create a lasting impact!

job.title: Contracts & Tenders Specialist - MedTech
job.description:

  • This company is large enough to invest in people and new technology, yet small enough to ensure that every single individual in the business can drive real change for good.
  • Everyone is driven and focused, and they care. They believe in what they do because they know what they do matters. 
  • Ambition is encouraged. They want you to be the best you can be and they will support you to drive your own development and carve your own path.
  • They believe in rewarding talent. So, if you perform well, are truly engaged and keen to make an impact, there will be no shortage of opportunities for you to achieve success.
WHAT YOU WILL LEAD AND GROW
  • This Tender & Contracts Specialist position is responsible for managing the end-to-end tender process, from pre-qualification and planning through to bid submission, contract award and engagement close-out.
  • Project managing tender responses to ensure submissions are tailored to customer requirements, accurate, compliant and delivered within strict deadlines is key to this role.
  • The position will prepare, coordinate and review contracts, customer agreements, extensions and variations across business units and geographical territories.
  • You will manage the tender calendar and tracking systems, keeping stakeholders informed of key dates, progress, outcomes and required actions.
  • You will be coordinating customer clarifications, questions, best and final offers, and requests for samples, ensuring timely and consistent responses.
  • You will act as a point of contact for customer enquiries relating to tenders and contracts, providing accurate information and escalating more complex matters when needed.
  • You will be preparing quote documentation based on approved requests and maintain accurate records within the quotes database.
  • You will be supporting the development and maintenance of tender and contract procedures, templates, forms and supporting documentation to meet business and audit requirements.
  • You will be preparing reports and summaries on tender, contract and quoting activity, including performance data and tender wins and losses, to support business decision-making.
  • You will be working closely with commercial and functional teams to gather input, complete actions and meet submission and contract deadlines.
  • You will be reviewing tender, contract and quoting processes to identify opportunities to improve efficiency, consistency, compliance and the quality of submissions.
  • you will be supporting tender response and commercial strategies, using stakeholder insights and analysis to help position the business for successful outcomes.
YOU WILL HAVE THE FOLLOWING TO BE SUCCESSFUL
  • To be successful in this role, you will have around 3 years’ experience in a contracts and tenders role, ideally within healthcare, medical devices or another regulated industry.
  • A sound understanding of tendering, contract management and quoting processes, with experience coordinating tender submissions and contract activities from preparation through to submission or execution.
  • Strong project management skills, with the ability to manage competing deadlines, multiple workloads and input from a range of stakeholders.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to review information, identify risks and recommend practical solutions.
  • Excellent written and verbal English communication skills, including experience preparing clear business reports, briefs and tender documentation.
  • Strong attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy, confidentiality and compliance.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, Word and PowerPoint.
  • A degree in Business, Management or Finance, or equivalent relevant industry experience.

job.title: Senior Biomedical Engineer | Medical Devices
job.description:
THE COMPANY YOU WOULD BE JOINING
  • This medical device company has been supporting surgeons, doctors and clinicians for over 60 years and has grown into a worldwide manufacturer and distributor of some of the best medical technology in their niche space.
  • This organisation combines their expertise in medical devices with software solutions to achieve integration in the operating theatre environment and to support clinical procedures and resource management.
WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU
  • This company offers you amazing opportunities to actually make an impact.
  • They consistently challenge and support their people’s personal and professional development.
  • They are always interested in recruiting great people to enable them to continue to play a pioneering role as a leading manufacturer of medical devices and medical technology.
WHAT YOU WILL LEAD AND GROW
  • This Senior Biomedical Engineer position, based in Auckland, NZ is responsible for managing the end-to-end service and operational delivery of biomedical equipment across New Zealand, including overseeing the NZ workshop and ensuring the full-service lifecycle for customer accounts is delivered efficiently and to a high standard.
  • The role involves performing complex technical repairs and maintenance, while also handling administrative and logistical aspects of service operations, operating with a high degree of independence in daily decision-making. The manager of this role is based in Sydney.
  • The position will oversee the day-to-day operations of the New Zealand workshop, including equipment intake, job prioritisation, and maintaining an organised and efficient workspace, along with maintaining accurate and up-to-date service records, job tracking, and work orders within SAP and the Quality Management System, ensuring all documentation is audit-ready at all times.
  • You will inspect, test, and repair loan and demonstration equipment to ensure availability meets the needs of the sales and customer teams and drive a proactive and strategic approach to asset lifecycle management by identifying aging equipment, prioritising service or replacement needs, and aligning actions with customer requirements and service contract commitments.
  • You will conduct safety and performance testing of equipment in compliance with applicable regulatory standards, including ANZ 3551, and internal company requirements and deliver both preventative maintenance and responsive repair services across the New Zealand hospital customer base to ensure optimal equipment performance and reliability.
  • You will diagnose and resolve complex technical issues independently, escalating where necessary to ensure timely and effective resolution and install and validate software updates, manage system integrations, and troubleshoot related issues to maintain and enhance overall equipment functionality and performance.
  • You will apply sound knowledge of hospital and surgical environments, including relevant standards such as AS/NZS 3551 and AS/NZS 3200 and demonstrate working knowledge of ISO 13485 and its application within medical device servicing and quality processes.
WHAT EXPERIENCE & SKILLS WILL YOU NEED TO GET THE JOB?
  • A degree or diploma in Biomedical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • 5+ years’ experience in biomedical engineering or a medical device service role in the medical device industry.
  • EWRB registration (EST/Electrician) with MCPA endorsement, or willingness to obtain.
  • Experience in the installation, maintenance, and servicing of capital medical equipment.
  • Exposure to laser equipment, particularly in testing and validation, is highly desirable, but not mandatory.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently and manage a regional workload with minimal supervision.
  • A full, current New Zealand driver’s licence and legal eligibility to work in New Zealand.
  • Strong technical troubleshooting, diagnostic and problem-solving skills.
  • Experience working within hospital/clinical environments and relevant medical device quality standards.
INTERESTED?
